rows.verified: The Food Standards Agency guidance covers provision of allergen information and best-practice allergen handling.
Food businesses must provide allergen information for foods containing regulated allergens.
Allergens present in prepacked food must be emphasised when they appear in the ingredients list.
Non-prepacked food requires allergen information for each item containing any of the 14 regulated allergens.
Prepacked-for-direct-sale food must meet applicable ingredient and allergen-labelling requirements.
Businesses should have processes for checking allergenic ingredients and controlling cross-contact.
Staff training and allergen checklists support reliable allergen communication.
The official guidance and its linked decision tools are updated when requirements or implementation guidance changes.
Food-allergy risk depends on the allergen, dose, cross-contact, recipe, labelling, staff communication, consumer susceptibility and emergency response.
FSA allergen evidence is food-, ingredient-, process-, business-, consumer- and time-specific and is not an exact parcel-level allergic-reaction probability.

rows.source: MHRA medicine and medical-device safety communications
rows.verified: MHRA monitors medicines and medical devices throughout their marketed life for safety issues.

rows.source: MHRA medicine and medical-device safety communications
rows.verified: Safety monitoring uses Yellow Card reports, clinical and epidemiological studies, published literature, manufacturers and other regulators.

rows.source: MHRA medicine and medical-device safety communications
rows.verified: Device Safety Information can require healthcare providers, professionals or patients to act to reduce a potential device risk.

rows.source: MHRA medicine and medical-device safety communications
rows.verified: Field Safety Notices are issued by manufacturers or representatives to communicate device safety issues and corrective actions.

rows.source: MHRA medicine and medical-device safety communications
rows.verified: Field Safety Notices normally must be notified to MHRA before release unless urgent corrective action is required.

rows.source: MHRA medicine and medical-device safety communications
rows.verified: Safety communications may address recalls, withdrawals, new contraindications, warnings, maintenance changes, compatibility issues or software corrections.

rows.source: MHRA medicine and medical-device safety communications
rows.verified: MHRA reviews the strength and clinical relevance of evidence, exposure and options for risk mitigation.

rows.source: MHRA medicine and medical-device safety communications
rows.verified: MHRA may require product-information changes, additional risk-reduction measures, or in rare cases recall, suspension or withdrawal.

rows.source: MHRA medicine and medical-device safety communications
rows.verified: Medical-device risk depends on device model, indication, software, maintenance, user, patient, environment, corrective action and communication timing.

rows.source: MHRA medicine and medical-device safety communications
rows.verified: MHRA safety evidence is product-, incident-, user-, patient-, corrective-action- and time-specific and is not an exact parcel-level harm probability.
A RIDDOR report is required only when an accident is work related and results in a reportable outcome.
Work-related deaths are reportable subject to the stated exceptions.
Specified reportable injuries include most fractures, amputations, permanent sight damage, serious crush injuries and qualifying burns.
Work-related incapacity lasting more than seven consecutive days can be reportable.
Certain diagnosed occupational diseases are reportable when the required work-related causal link exists.
Occupational cancers are reportable when linked to relevant workplace carcinogen or mutagen exposure.
Diseases linked to occupational exposure to biological agents can be reportable.
Specified dangerous occurrences and qualifying gas incidents are reportable under the applicable RIDDOR provisions.
RIDDOR applicability depends on employment status, work relationship, diagnosis, injury type, duration, causation and the specific regulatory category.
HSE RIDDOR guidance is incident-, worker-, diagnosis-, causation-, reporting-rule- and time-specific and is not an exact parcel-level accident probability.
